content.overview: Section 128 provides that the liability of the surety is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor, unless it is otherwise provided by the contract. The statutory illustration shows that a surety guaranteeing payment of a bill of exchange is liable not only for the amount of the bill but also for any interest and charges that have become due on it when the bill is dishonoured.
content.glance: Surety's liability is co-extensive with the principal debtor's unless the contract provides otherwise.
content.study: The liability of the surety is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor, unless it is otherwise provided by the contract. Co-extensive means the surety is ordinarily liable to the same extent as the principal debtor for the guaranteed obligation. The contract may limit or qualify that liability. Illustration: A guarantees to B the payment of a bill of exchange by C, the acceptor. The bill is dishonoured by C. A is liable not only for the amount of the bill but also for any interest and charges which may have become due on it. Current-law framing: identify the guaranteed obligation, check whether the contract provides otherwise, and apply the co-extensive rule (including incidental liabilities illustrated by the statute) only where the contract does not restrict it.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: The liability of the surety is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor, unless it is otherwise provided by the contract.

sections.heading: Statutory illustration
sections.body: A guarantees to B the payment of a bill of exchange by C, the acceptor. The bill is dishonoured by C. A is liable not only for the amount of the bill but also for any interest and charges which may have become due on it.

sections.heading: Contractual qualification
sections.body: The co-extensive rule yields where the contract of guarantee provides otherwise. The actual terms of the guarantee control the extent of liability.

sections.heading: Relationship to neighbouring sections
sections.body: Section 126 defines the guarantee and parties. Section 127 concerns consideration. Section 128 states the default extent of liability. Continuing guarantees and revocation are addressed in Sections 129–131.

examples.title: Bill of exchange illustration
examples.body: A guarantees to B payment of a bill of exchange accepted by C. On dishonour, A is liable for the bill amount plus interest and charges that have become due, matching the statutory illustration, unless the guarantee provides otherwise.

examples.title: Limited guarantee
examples.body: If the contract expressly limits the surety's liability to a stated sum, that contractual limit applies and the co-extensive rule does not expand liability beyond the agreed cap.

hypotheticals.question: A guarantees B's debt to C without any limitation. B defaults. To what extent is A liable?
hypotheticals.analysis: Under Section 128 the surety's liability is co-extensive with the principal debtor's unless the contract provides otherwise. On these facts the surety is liable to the same extent as the principal debtor.

hypotheticals.question: The guarantee expressly caps the surety's liability at a fixed sum. Does Section 128 override the cap?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 128 applies the co-extensive rule only unless it is otherwise provided by the contract. The contractual limit controls.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 128 states that the liability of the surety is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor, unless it is otherwise provided by the contract. The statutory illustration confirms that, on dishonour of a bill of exchange guaranteed by the surety, the surety is liable not only for the amount of the bill but also for interest and charges that have become due. The co-extensive rule is the default; any contractual qualification or limitation controls. Section 128 addresses extent of liability; it does not define the guarantee (Section 126) or address consideration (Section 127).
examples: Bill of exchange: surety liable for amount plus interest and charges on dishonour, per the statutory illustration, unless the contract provides otherwise.
Contractual cap: where the guarantee limits liability to a stated sum, the co-extensive rule does not override that limit.
distinctions: Section 128 concerns the extent of the surety's liability; Section 126 defines the guarantee and parties.
Section 127 concerns consideration for the guarantee and is a separate question.
The co-extensive rule yields to any contrary provision in the contract of guarantee.
